Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Waste generated (kg)

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

assignment_context:
Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

assignment_context:
Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

assignment_context:
Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Vehicle emission

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

· Waste generated (kg)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

· Vehicle emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly

Assignment Title: CARBON EMISSIONS

Assignment Question:
A city encourages its citizens to monitor their daily carbon emissions. Every individual enters information about their daily activities, and a Java program estimates their daily carbon footprint.

The program should use Java operators (arithmetic, relational, logical, and assignment operators) to calculate emissions and determine whether the person qualifies as an Eco-Friendly Citizen.

The estimated carbon emissions are calculated using the following rules:

· Each mile driven by a petrol vehicle emits 0.40 kg CO₂

· Each kWh of electricity consumed emits 0.85 kg CO₂

· Each kilogram of waste generated emits 1.20 kg CO₂

The program should also consider two eco-friendly habits:

· Recycling today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

· Used public transport today (1 = Yes, 0 = No)

A person is considered an Eco-Friendly Citizen if:

· Total carbon footprint is less than 20 kg CO₂, AND the person recycled, AND the person used public transport.

Input

The program receives:

· Miles driven

· Electricity consumed (kWh)

· Waste generated (kg)

· Recycled? (1/0)

· Used public transport? (1/0)

Formula:

Vehicle Emission = miles × 0.40

Electricity Emission = electricity × 0.85

Waste Emission = waste × 1.20

Total Carbon Footprint = Vehicle Emission + Electricity Emission +Waste Emission

Expected Output

· Vehicle emission

· Electricity emission

· Waste emission

· Total carbon footprint

· Whether the target (<20 kg) is achieved

· Whether the citizen is Eco-Friendly
